issues.legal_issue: The fraud-or-mistake postponement rule does not apply to the limitation period for an application challenging an arbitral award under a procedure that fixes its own outer time limit.
material_facts: The parties received the arbitral award, but the application challenging it was filed 236 days later.
The objectors sought to postpone limitation under the fraud-or-mistake rule, alleging that subsequent negotiations and an agreement had delayed their challenge.
The award-challenge procedure provided a defined period and only a limited extension, ending with an express outer boundary.
issues.conclusion: The fraud-or-mistake rule is excluded from determining limitation for an application to set aside an arbitral award under Section 34; the remand and the order condoning the delay were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 29(2) of the Limitation Act, provisions in Sections 4–24 apply to a special-law limitation period only to the extent they are not expressly excluded; exclusion may be inferred from the special law’s language, scheme, and object. Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act supplies both the commencement point and a defined outer limit for challenging an award, and applying Section 17 of the Limitation Act would conflict with that limit, the finality and speed the Arbitration Act seeks to secure, and the enforcement scheme in Section 36. The Court relied on Vidyacharan Shukla v. Khubchand Baghel, Hukumdev Narain Yadav v. Lalit Narain Mishra, Commissioner of Customs and Central Excise v. Hongo India (P) Ltd., Union of India v. Popular Construction Co., Chhattisgarh State Electricity Board v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission, and Gopal Sardar v. Karuna Sardar.

predicates.award_challenge_proceeding: A party has brought a proceeding to challenge an arbitral award.
predicates.award_effectively_received: The party challenging the award has effectively received it.
predicates.procedure_has_fixed_outer_challenge_limi: The procedure for challenging the award sets a defined challenge period and a limited extension with an express outer boundary.

issues.definition: When a party effectively receives an award in a proceeding governed by a fixed outer challenge limit, the fraud-deferral rule does not apply to postpone that limit.

issues.legal_issue: Fraud alleged after effective receipt of an arbitral award does not postpone limitation when the objector already knows of the award and has the facts needed to challenge it.
material_facts: The objectors received the award before the alleged memorandum of understanding was made.
The objectors knew of the award and had the right to challenge it upon receipt.
The alleged fraud concerned subsequent negotiations and failure to perform the agreement, not fraudulent delivery or concealment of the award.
issues.conclusion: Once the award was effectively received, subsequent alleged fraud did not defer the commencement of limitation; the fraud-or-mistake rule applies to concealment of knowledge or necessary material, not merely to conduct that impedes exercising a known right.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1)(b) and (d) of the Limitation Act address fraud that conceals knowledge of the right or a document necessary to establish it; once the claimant knows the facts necessary to pursue the remedy, limitation runs. Section 17 does not cover every kind of fraud or mere prevention from exercising a known right. Yeswant Deorao Deshmukh v. Walchand Ramchand Kothari distinguishes concealing knowledge of a right from preventing its exercise, and Pallav Sheth v. Custodian describes the rule as protecting a party from failing to proceed when necessary facts or material have been willfully concealed. Under Union of India v. Tecco Trichy Engineers & Contractors, delivery must amount to effective receipt; fraud in delivery means the receipt requirement itself is not satisfied.

rule.if: award_challenge_proceeding and award_effectively_received and objector_knew_facts_needed_to_challenge and alleged_fraud_did_not_conceal_the_award_or_necessary_material

predicates.award_challenge_proceeding: A party has brought a proceeding to challenge an arbitral award.
predicates.award_effectively_received: The party challenging the award has effectively received it.
predicates.objector_knew_facts_needed_to_challenge: The objector knew the award and the facts necessary to pursue a challenge.
predicates.alleged_fraud_did_not_conceal_the_award_: The alleged fraud did not conceal delivery of the award or material needed to know and pursue the challenge.

issues.definition: When an objector effectively receives an award, knows the facts needed to challenge it, and the alleged fraud concealed neither the award nor necessary material, that fraud does not postpone limitation.
